method: Descriptive stacked before-after event study with incident fixed effects
pre_hours: same as post, excluding known Reddit incident hours

events.timing_basis: Analyst proxy, 03:00 Moscow; company says overnight Oct 7-8; reports place complaints around 02:00 Moscow and network deterioration by 04:00. Sweep midnight-06:00 Moscow, not a confidence interval.
Analyst proxy, 06:00 Moscow; primary company statement says morning, some reports say overnight. Exact time unverified. Sweep midnight-noon Moscow, not a confidence interval.

Analyst proxy, 04:00 Moscow; first official alert visible at 01:12 UTC, secondary monitoring reports interruption around 03:45 Moscow. Sweep midnight-06:00 Moscow, not a confidence interval. Alert time is not strike time.

outcome: log1p(hourly posts+comments) minus mean log1p at the identical UTC hour 7,14,21 days earlier
percentage_change: 100*((observed_post/expected_post)/(observed_pre/expected_pre)-1); expected is sum of arithmetic means at identical hours 7,14,21 days earlier
pooled_r: Within-incident weighted Pearson correlation of post indicator and adjusted log activity; each incident total weight 1. This is partial r controlling for incident intercepts, not correlation between only three event totals.
benchmark_check: Subtract per-hour median adjusted log activity among baseline>=100/day series; leave each target out of its own benchmark. This is a broad-sample sensitivity, not a proven untreated control.
repeat_rule: Negative r and negative percentage change for every separate incident. Stronger sensitivity flag requires this at every swept start time for both 10h/12h and with/without broad-sample adjustment.
ranking_rule: Lowest primary 12h pooled r among nominal 3/3 decreases; stronger timing-stability category shown separately. No tuning of anchor or length to maximize correlation.
inference: Descriptive only. No IID-hour p values, no causal confidence intervals: only 3 nearby incidents, uncertain timing, possible carryover, and exploratory selection across 1221 targets. Timing ranges are scenario ranges, not confidence intervals.
